findings.source: LoanManager.sol:879 while (next_ != 0 && paymentDueDate_ >= sortedPayments[next_].paymentDueDate) { current_ = next_; next_ = sortedPayments[current_].next; }
findings.issue: The loop condition is a loop-carried boolean computed once before the loop and again at the end of the body from the next values, so the header reads 'while _248' and the condition is written twice.
findings.rule: If the header tests a variable whose entry value is f(x0) and whose back-edge value is f(x_next), with f free of side effects and no store in the body to what f reads, print 'while f(x):' with the loop variables and drop the variable.

findings.issue: The source condition becomes an exit test at the top of 'while True' because four SSA copies are attached to the exit.
findings.rule: A leading 'if not c: <copies of loop variables>; break' is the loop condition 'while c'; apply the copies after the loop (they are renamings).
